title: Self-adjointness of product noise
statement: Let $[0m\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $[0m\pi$ be a probability mass function on $[0m\Omega$, and let $[0m\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of the real-valued functions on $[0m\Omega$ is given whose distinguished vector is the constant-one function and which is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $[0m\pi$. For any natural number $[0m n$, any $[0m\rho\in[0,1]$, and any real-valued functions $f,g$ on $[0m\Omega^n$, the product noise operator that independently retains each input coordinate with probability $[0m\rho$ and otherwise resamples it from $[0m\pi$ is self-adjoint for the product inner product weighted by $[0m\pi^n$: $[0m\langle f,T_\rho g\rangle=[0m\langle T_\rho f,g\rangle$.
hypotheses_covered: A basis of functions on $[0m\Omega$ with constant-one distinguished vector and $[0m\pi$-orthonormality
